hooks.text: Marine biologists accidentally killed the oldest living animal known to science.
How did a routine ocean study destroy a five-hundred-year life?
Five hundred and seven years of life ended in a shipboard freezer.

title: Scientists killed the oldest clam by accident
description: Researchers in 2006 dredged an ocean quahog clam off Iceland and accidentally ended its 507-year life in a shipboard freezer.

beats.text: Marine biologists accidentally killed the oldest living animal known to science.
beats.visual: Live ocean quahog clam Arctica islandica on the seafloor, 2006

beats.text: In 2006, researchers from Bangor University were dredging the cold seafloor off the northern coast of Iceland.
beats.visual: Map of the northern coast of Iceland, bathymetry map

beats.text: They collected an ordinary ocean quahog clam and immediately froze it solid along with all their other samples.
beats.visual: Scientific ocean sampling equipment and benthic dredge on a research vessel

beats.text: Only after later slicing the thick shell open in the laboratory did they discover its astonishing true age.
beats.visual: Close-up of annual growth rings on a mollusk shell cross section microscope

beats.text: Named Ming by journalists, the unfortunate animal had been quietly alive since 1499 during the Ming dynasty.
beats.visual: Ming Dynasty emperor portrait and period artifacts

beats.text: Precise carbon-14 dating later proved it had amazingly survived for five hundred and seven years.
beats.visual: A researcher using a diamond saw to cut a shell in a laboratory
